published_statement: p.4: 'The proton mass is proportional to Lambda_QCD (M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD), therefore, the measurements of the variation of the electron-to-proton mass ratio mu = m_e/M_p is equivalent to the measurements of the variation of X_e = m_e/Lambda_QCD.' (verbatim as READ by sibling audit 0705.3704; the tree quotes the first clause at address.py:445-446.)
published_hypotheses: P1 chiral-limit proportionality: quark-mass contributions to M_p are not written; the 'therefore' (mu equivalent to X_e) is exact only if M_p/Lambda_QCD is independent of m_q/Lambda_QCD (machine-checked: residual is -S d ln X_q, check C1).
P2 '~3' is an approximate number with no scheme, flavour number or loop order stated for Lambda_QCD (none given in the READ text, per sibling audit).

P3 units convention: 'One can only measure the variation of dimensionless quantities' (p.4, per sibling audit) -- masses are expressed in units of Lambda_QCD (X_e, X_q, X_s); Flambaum-Wiringa 0807.4943 p.1 (READ by sibling) makes it explicit: 'convenient to assume that Lambda_QCD is constant ... measure all masses and energies in units of Lambda_QCD'.

P4 the paper does NOT state that Lambda_QCD is physically independent of the Higgs vev; its sec. V GUT discussion lets Lambda_QCD vary with alpha (d Lambda/Lambda ~ 34 d alpha/alpha, 'model dependent', per sibling audit).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (attribution) address.py:445-446 labels the sentence 'this project's H2'; address.py:104 defines H2 as 'Lambda_QCD ITSELF FIXED: d ln m_p/d ln v = S'. Machine-checked (checks B1, B2): in the chiral limit m_p/Lambda_3 is v-independent under H1 (Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27), d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9) exactly as under H2, while K_mu = -7/9 (H1) vs -1 (H2). The READ sentence therefore holds under both hypotheses and does not discriminate them; 'Lambda independent of v' is a premise the tree adds, not the sentence's content. Flambaum's 'Lambda_QCD constant' is a units convention (P3), which cannot by itself fix how Lambda responds to v.

Machine-checked: Euler homogeneity (A1), H2 gives S exactly (A2), H1 gives 2/9 + 7S/9 (A5). The tree is strictly more general than the sentence here.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What Flambaum had in 2007: the chiral-limit picture M_p ~ Lambda_QCD, an approximate '~3', older sigma-term estimates (sigma_piN ~45-60 MeV, sigma_s poorly known), alpha_s(M_Z) ~ 0.118 (essentially today's value). What came later: lattice sigma terms (FLAG 2024: S_uds = 0.093-0.109), N3LO heavy-quark matrix elements (Hill-Solon 2014), lattice proton-mass decomposition (chiQCD 2018), and a 0.1180(9) alpha_s average. Does any of it change the conclusion? EVIDENCE AGAINST M's hypothesis for this sentence: the proportionality is a consequence of dimensional transmutation and holds exactly in the chiral limit whatever the data (A1, B1); the '~3' is reproduced from today's alpha_s (2.6-2.8 for n_f = 3, 3.1-3.2 for n_f = 4, computed) and alpha_s has not moved materially since 2007; the later sigma-term data bound the dropped correction at 4.5-10.9% of d ln X_q, which the sentence's '~' already admits. EVIDENCE FOR a limitation (not a data gap): the sentence is chiral-limit and scheme-unspecified, and it is silent on how Lambda_QCD responds to v -- that is a question about physics above the electroweak scale, not missing data, and the tree correctly refuses to resolve it (address.py:331-334). No datum the authors lacked changes this conclusion.
grade_evidence: The published statement STANDS as what it is: M_p proportional to Lambda_QCD is exact in the chiral limit by dimensional homogeneity (sympy A1), the correction is the Feynman-Hellmann S (C1: residual -S d ln X_q, 4.5-10.9% on FLAG 2024 inputs), and '~3' is reproduced as M_p/Lambda_MSbar = 2.62-2.83 (n_f=3), 2.92-3.24 (n_f=4) at 2-4 loops from alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1180 (computed; convention-dependent, 2.5-11.3 over n_f and loop order). NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree uses it for more than it says: address.py:445-446 labels the sentence 'this project's H2' and address.py:104 defines H2 as 'Lambda_QCD ITSELF FIXED' as v varies. Machine-checked (B1-B2): the proportionality holds identically under H1 (d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9) and H2, which differ in K_mu (-7/9 vs -1); so the source supports the m_p = Lambda F structure common to both, not H2. Flambaum's own 'Lambda constant' is a units convention (0807.4943 p.1, READ by sibling). Consequences are bounded: the tree names H2 as a hypothesis, refuses H1 vs H2 (address.py:331-334, 461) and reports both, and never consumes the factor 3 (E1), so no tree number moves. Not WRONG: no counterexample, the sentence is true as written. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no moved datum moves the proportionality or the '~3'. SOURCE LIMIT, stated: the paper was not re-opened in this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted; arXiv egress-blocked); the verbatim statement rests on the sibling audit's in-docket READ of all 8 pages, matched word for word by the tree's own quotation.
what_would_change_the_grade: (1) A direct re-read of 0705.3704v2 p.3-4 finding that Flambaum DOES assert Lambda_QCD independent of the Higgs vev (not merely as a unit convention) would move this to STANDS for the attribution. (2) If the tree began consuming the factor 3 numerically, its scheme/n_f would have to be named (2.6 for n_f=3 vs 4.5 for n_f=5 at 4 loops). (3) Reading Calmet 1707.06922 (or another source) that states H2 as physics would supply the literature support the tree's 'BOTH ARE IN THE LITERATURE' (address.py:106-107) claims, without changing this entry's grade, which concerns what 0705.3704 says. (4) Nothing currently conceivable in data moves the proportionality itself.
